sections.h2: Where is Lancaster County, SC, and what is in it?
sections.html:
Lancaster County sits in the Piedmont along the North Carolina line and is part of the Charlotte metropolitan area. The county seat is the City of Lancaster, and Indian Land, in the northern panhandle, is a large unincorporated community with 32,759 residents in 2020.

The county covers 555.05 square miles, of which 549.07 are land. The Catawba River and Sugar Creek form its western edge and the Lynches River its eastern edge. It borders Mecklenburg and Union counties in North Carolina and Chesterfield, Kershaw, Fairfield, Chester and York counties in South Carolina.

The 2020 census counted 96,016 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 114,296. The county was created in 1785, and settlers arrived in the early 1750s. The Battle of Waxhaws was fought near the state line during the Revolutionary War. The Catawba people lived in the area before settlers came, and early settlers were mostly Scots-Irish Presbyterians.

sections.h2: Who collects property tax in Lancaster County?
sections.html:
The Lancaster County Treasurer collects current property taxes and acts as the county's banker, from the County Administration Building at 101 North Main Street in Lancaster. Past-due real property goes to the Tax Collector's Office after the March deadline.

sections.h2: When are Lancaster County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Real estate and personal property taxes are due January 15 without penalty, and if that date falls on a weekend or holiday the due date moves to 5 pm the next business day. The county mails bills at least 30 days before the due date.

After March 16, unless it falls on a weekend or holiday, unpaid property taxes go to the Tax Collector's Office. Motor vehicle bills follow a separate schedule: they are due on the last day of the month and are mailed 30 days before.

The Treasurer's page does not list the percentage penalties. State law sets them, with a first penalty after the due date, more added in February, and more added in March. Section 12-45-180 covers the schedule, and says a postmark decides if a mailed payment is on time. Call the Treasurer for the exact figures for your bill.

  • If property changed owners during the tax year and the new owner never got a timely notice, the statute requires the treasurer to waive the penalties.
  • A mailed payment with the wrong postmark can be excused with proof.

sections.h2: How does a Lancaster County assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
State law governs the process, and it begins with a written objection to the County Assessor within 90 days after the assessment notice is mailed. We could not open a Lancaster County assessor page, so use the state steps below and ask the office for its forms.

  1. Ask the Assessor for a conference, which should be scheduled within 30 days.
  2. File a written protest within 30 days after the conference.
  3. Receive the Assessor's written response, usually within 30 days.
  4. Appeal to the county board within 30 days of that response.
  5. Request a contested case hearing before the Administrative Law Court within 30 days of the board's decision.

If the matter is still open on December 31, the bill is adjusted to 80 percent of the protested value until the case ends. The full text is in Sections 12-60-2510 to 12-60-2550.

Under Section 12-43-217, counties reappraise on a five-year cycle and must notify owners of value or class changes of $1,000 or more.

sections.h2: What is the 4 percent legal residence rate in Lancaster County?
sections.html:
A legal residence that the owner occupies, with up to five contiguous acres, is taxed on 4 percent of fair market value. Apply on or before the first penalty date for the first year you claim it. The home may not be rented for more than 72 days a year.

When you sell, the buyer must file for their own rate. Wrongly claiming it brings a penalty equal to 100 percent of the tax paid plus interest. Farm land can qualify at 4 percent too, with rollback taxes for the current year and three prior years if the use changes. See Chapter 43 of Title 12.

sections.h2: What makes Indian Land different from the rest of Lancaster County?
sections.html:
Indian Land is an unincorporated community with no downtown, located about six miles east of Fort Mill, and it had 32,759 residents in 2020. U.S. 521 and SC 160 are the main roads, and there is no public transportation. A 2014 overlay district sets design rules for new construction along those corridors.

In March 2018 voters rejected incorporation by 83 percent. Its schools include Indian Land Elementary, Harrisburg and Van Wyck elementaries, middle and intermediate schools, and Indian Land High School, with a new high school opened in August 2021. The University of South Carolina Lancaster began offering classes there in 2018.

  • Indian Land is not a town, so a house there is served by county offices.
  • Sellers of acreage should ask whether agricultural classification applies.

sections.h2: Which other Lancaster County offices matter when you sell?
sections.html:
The county's main number is 803-285-1565, and the County Administration Building at 101 North Main Street houses the offices most sellers need. The county website lists Development Services and a Code of Ordinances for permit and zoning questions, and it posts meeting notices for the Planning Commission and the Indian Land Consolidated Fire Protection District Commission.

  • Treasurer: current taxes and payment.
  • Tax Collector: past-due real property after the March deadline.
  • Assessor: value, classification and appeals.
  • Development Services: permits and land use.

On the deed itself, South Carolina charges $1.85 per $500 of value, with $1.30 going to the state and $0.55 to the county, and the seller is generally liable. Foreclosure and deed in lieu transfers to a mortgage holder are exempt. The register's own recording fee is separate, and we did not confirm it for Lancaster County. The rules are in Title 12, Chapter 24.

sections.h2: How strong is the Lancaster County economy?
sections.html:
Lancaster County had 24,479 employed people in the third quarter of 2023, with an average annual wage of $58,427. Health care and social assistance led with 3,846 jobs, followed by retail trade at 3,648, manufacturing at 2,796, professional and technical services at 2,239, and accommodation and food service at 2,208. Food Lion and Walmart are among the largest employers.

County GDP in 2022 was $4.3 billion.

faqs.q: When are Lancaster County property taxes due?
faqs.a: January 15 is the due date for real estate and personal property taxes without penalty, with the date moving to the next business day if it lands on a weekend or holiday. Bills are mailed at least 30 days earlier.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Lancaster County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay at 101 N Main Street in Lancaster, online at lancastersctax.qpaybill.com, by phone at 803-797-2853, or by mail to P.O. Box 729, Lancaster, SC 29720.

faqs.q: What happens to unpaid taxes after March 16 in Lancaster County?
faqs.a: They go to the Tax Collector's Office, reachable at 803-283-8885. Call it for a payoff figure before a sale.

faqs.q: Is there a fee for paying Lancaster County tax by card?
faqs.a: Yes. Card payments carry a 2.35 percent convenience fee that goes to the service provider, not the county. A returned payment costs $30.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a Lancaster County assessment?
faqs.a: Send the County Assessor a written objection within 90 days after the assessment notice is mailed, then follow the protest and board steps. Ask the Assessor's office for its forms.
